# Model card — Whirr acoustic activity classifier

**Model family:** deterministic multinomial logistic regression over frozen spectral features  
**Schema:** `whirr.model.v1` with optional `whirr.soundprint.v1`  
**Feature contract:** `whirr-features-v1`  
**Bundled artifact:** `models/whirr-reference-fan.json`  
**Bundled status:** READY  
**Provenance:** `SYNTHETIC_REFERENCE`  
**Last evaluation:** generated by `npm run eval:reference`; see [`evaluation.md`](evaluation.md) for the live numbers and hashes.

> **Critical scope statement.** The bundled model is trained on **procedurally synthesised audio**, not on a physical fan or any real appliance. Its metrics are real measurements of that synthetic dataset and demonstrate the training/evaluation pipeline. They are **not** field accuracy and must not be cited as evidence that Whirr recognizes a physical object reliably. A user-calibrated model recorded from the actual object in its actual environment is required for any real-world accuracy claim.

## 1. Intended use

- Distinguish confident operation of **one taught object** from idle/background sound in a **supervised** setting.
- Produce a conservative, precision-first state timeline used to calculate billable active time.
- Demonstrate that a commodity microphone plus local classical ML can act as a software-defined usage meter without modifying the object.
- Support operator review, renter disputes and reproducible offline evaluation.

## 2. Out-of-scope use

- Unattended access control, locks, theft prevention or “tamper-proof” billing.
- Identifying which of two identical machines is running.
- Universal appliance recognition. A model is specific to the object, microphone placement, room and recording conditions used in calibration.
- Safety-critical monitoring, fault diagnosis, predictive maintenance or electrical protection.
- Detecting speaker playback of a recording. A microphone can be fooled; the system is designed to refuse ambiguous time, not to win an anti-spoof arms race.
- Inferring speech content, identity, occupancy or any other personal attribute. No speech recognition, speaker identification or semantic audio model is used.

## 3. Inputs and features

Audio is resampled to **16 kHz mono** in the browser. Analysis uses a 2048-sample Hann-windowed frame (128 ms) with a 512-sample hop (32 ms). Each frame produces 21 finite features:

`log_rms`, `zero_cross_rate`, `spectral_centroid`, `spectral_spread`, `spectral_rolloff`, `spectral_flatness`, `spectral_flux`, `crest_factor`, `dominant_frequency`, `harmonic_ratio`, eight logarithmic band energies (`50–120`, `120–250`, `250–500`, `500–1000`, `1000–2000`, `2000–4000`, `4000–6000`, `6000–7800 Hz`), `spectral_slope`, `peak_amplitude`, `low_high_ratio`.

Quality flags are **not** model features but gate usability: `CLIPPED` (peak ≥ 0.98), `SILENT` (RMS < 1e-5), `LOW_LEVEL` (RMS < 0.0015), plus `GAP`, `DEVICE_LOST` and `TAB_HIDDEN` generated by the session pipeline. Any disqualifying flag forces the frame to be non-billable (`UNCERTAIN` or ignored in training).

Raw audio is **not** uploaded. Calibration takes upload only the 21-dimensional feature vectors, per-frame flags, duration and provenance. Live sessions upload only sealed state intervals.

## 4. Model

- Three classes: `idle`, `active`, `other` (negative/background/transition).
- Features are standardised using training-fold means and standard deviations. Standardisation is stored inside the artifact.
- Balanced class weights compensate for unequal frame counts.
- Full-batch gradient descent with momentum, learning rate 0.14, L2 1e-4, deterministic seed `0x5eed`; the final reference fits 600 iterations. No stochastic sampling and no external pretrained weights.
- The active threshold is selected from 0.50–0.99 in 0.01 steps by a precision-first objective: maximise recall subject to precision penalties and false-billable penalties.
- The acoustic passport is fitted from the same usable calibration frames, as a separate post-classifier consistency guard. It is not part of the held-out activity metrics.
- Frozen decision policy for the reference: EMA smoothing 0.45, `onFrames` 4, `offFrames` 5, idle threshold 0.50, active margin 0.10. Threshold is stored in the artifact; the shipped reference selected **0.82**.
- Inference is a pure function of the artifact and feature vector, so the browser and Node replay produce the same prediction for the same input.

## 5. Training data provenance

The bundled dataset is generated by `scripts/generate-fixtures.ts`:

- 16 synthetic takes covering idle room tone, fan-like broadband/tonal noise at different gains and modulation, a hair-dryer-like high-frequency source, speech-like harmonics, music-like tones, kettle-like tones, clatter and vacuum-like noise.
- The labelled replay fixture is **55 s**: 5 s idle · 15 s running · 10 s idle · 20 s running · 5 s idle.
- Noise is seeded, so regeneration is deterministic. The dataset hash is stored in the artifact and reported in the evaluation.
- There are **no real-object recordings**, no internet audio, no third-party datasets and no personal data in the bundled artifact.
- User calibration takes are recorded in the operator's browser with explicit microphone activation. Only features and quality flags are stored; raw audio is discarded. Operators can delete individual takes or purge all calibration data.

## 6. Evaluation method

**Session-level leave-one-take-out.** For each take, a model is trained on all other takes, standardised on those folds, and used to score every frame of the held-out take. No frame is scored by a model that saw another frame from the same take. The threshold is tuned on those held-out predictions, then a final model is fitted on all usable frames.

Metrics reported by the artifact:

- **Precision** — of all billed active time, the fraction that was truly active.
- **Recall** — of all true active duration, the fraction billed.
- **False billable time (FBT)** — billed active time on non-active takes divided by all non-active duration.
- **Frame accuracy** — argmax accuracy, reported but not optimised.
- **Confusion matrix** — three classes over held-out frames.
- **Tuned log-RMS baseline** — a non-ML threshold included so the learned model can lose.

### Bundled reference result (synthetic, held-out takes)

| Metric | Value |
| --- | ---: |
| Status | **READY** |
| Precision | **96.30%** |
| Recall | **97.16%** |
| False billable time | **1.804%** |
| Frame accuracy | 89.26% |
| Method | leave-one-take-out |
| Tuned RMS baseline precision / recall / FBT | 100.00% / 98.49% / 0.000% |

The learned model has **worse false-billable time than the tuned RMS baseline on this synthetic dataset**. That is reported rather than hidden. The baseline is unusually strong because the synthetic “active” source is much louder and spectrally distinct than idle. A real deployment should compare both and may legitimately choose the simpler baseline if it wins on that object's data. The current hysteresis/classifier pipeline is retained because it provides calibrated multi-class probabilities, background rejection and a path to harder objects; that is a design hypothesis, not a proven advantage.

## 7. Acoustic passport

Every trained model also contains a `whirr.soundprint.v1` artifact. It converts the eight log-band energies into an amplitude-invariant spectral shape, stores the mean active profile and mean idle/negative profile, and computes cosine similarity for each live frame.

- The threshold is selected from the calibration score distribution: just below the active 10th percentile and above the non-active 95th percentile. A gate is enrolled only when it keeps at least 85% of active calibration frames while rejecting at least 80% of non-active profiles.
- When the gate is active, a confidently active frame below the threshold gets `SOUNDPRINT_MISMATCH`; hysteresis disqualifies the frame, so it becomes `UNCERTAIN` and cannot contribute to the bill. The gate can only reduce billing, never create a charge.
- When the calibration profiles overlap too much, the passport is `WEAK` and the identity gate is disabled rather than guessed. Models trained before the passport are still valid and simply have no soundprint.
- This is an **enrollment-fit consistency guard**, not a held-out identity classifier or anti-spoofing. The held-out activity metrics do not include the passport. Similar machines, room changes and recorded playback can pass.
- The public passport page includes a **local-only probe**: after a microphone gesture, the browser computes the same band-shape cosine similarity from live frames. It starts no session, uploads nothing and changes no bill. It demonstrates the gate; it is not an independent identity test.

Reference passport (synthetic calibration, reported by `npm run eval:reference`):

| Metric | Value |
| --- | ---: |
| Status | **ENROLLED** |
| Match threshold | 91.48% |
| Active calibration median | 97.50% |
| Active 10th percentile | 93.48% |
| Non-active 95th percentile | 91.26% |
| Active frames blocked at threshold | 3.97% |
| Non-active frames passed at threshold | 4.37% |

## 8. Billing safety gate

A model is assigned:

- **READY** when held-out precision ≥ 95%, false billable ≤ 2%, and recall ≥ 40%.
- **LIMITED** when precision ≥ 85%, false billable ≤ 8%, and recall ≥ 35%. LIMITED models publish terms that require operator approval of every session's bill before capture.
- **REJECTED** when data requirements fail or metrics miss the LIMITED floor. A rejected model is stored but never activated; terms cannot be published.

Hard data failures include fewer than two idle takes, fewer than two active takes, no negative take, fewer than 60 usable frames per take, fewer than 120 idle or active frames total, a missing class, or almost no loudness separation between idle and active.

These thresholds are product policy, not a safety certification. They are deliberately conservative about false billing and allow unbilled uncertainty.

## 9. Limitations and failure modes

- **Synthetic provenance.** No claim of physical-object accuracy. Real recordings can be much harder than generated noise.
- **Replay spoofing.** A speaker playing a recording of the object can look active. The system cannot detect this reliably.
- **Similar machines.** One microphone cannot attribute sound to one of two identical devices running simultaneously. The passport compares spectral shape, not physical identity.
- **Passport calibration fit.** The gate is tuned on the same calibration takes it is evaluated against. Its reported retention/rejection rates are fit statistics, not held-out generalization. Narrow separation is surfaced in the artifact notes.
- **Acoustic drift.** Distance, fan speed, room echo, microphone model and background appliances change the distribution. Drift is not automatically detected; operators should recalibrate and review disputes.
- **Transition latency.** Hysteresis intentionally delays entry/exit. Short bursts may be unbilled; stopping may leave a short uncertain tail. This is biased toward the renter.
- **Background confusion.** A loud unrelated appliance can be `other` or, if acoustically similar, active. Negative takes and precision-first thresholds reduce but do not eliminate this.
- **No camera fusion.** No visual confirmation is implemented; camera visibility would not prove operation anyway.
- **Tab/device gaps.** Suspension, sleep, permission revocation or unplugging stops accrual. Free gaps are not a complete record of physical use.
- **No fairness guarantee.** The model is not audited across devices, rooms, hearing accessibility needs or demographics; acoustic features are not intended to encode people, but background speech is part of the negative class.

## 10. Ethical and privacy considerations

- Microphone use requires an explicit user gesture and browser permission. The app never opens the microphone on page load. The public probe follows the same rule and stops on cancel, disconnect or leaving the page.
- Only features and state intervals leave the browser. Raw audio is not stored by the server.
- Calibration is opt-in and purgeable. Consent records store hashes of IP/user-agent, not raw values.
- A renter sees the exact terms, model status, cap, uncertainty policy and limitations before approving.
- The system refuses to infer sensitive attributes and does not use speech recognition.
- Deployments must inform people nearby that acoustic sensing is active; the UI displays sensing state while a session runs.

## 10a. Whirr 2.0 additions: held-out validation and drift

A calibration can now mark takes as `TRAINING` or `VALIDATION`. Validation takes are never used to fit the model they evaluate. The Model Review surface reports a held-out report with take-level billable time, precision/recall where the labels permit it, and a plain-language “what would change this status” panel. If no validation takes exist, the status is `NOT_RUN`; it is not inferred from calibration fit.

After a session, the browser uploads a diagnostic summary of stored interval flags — mismatch duration, uncertainty and observed time. It is not audio and not billing evidence. The passport derives `FRESH`, `DRIFT_SUSPECTED` or `OVERDUE` from aggregate diagnostics and calibration age. Drift can prompt operator review or recalibration; it never retroactively changes a settled receipt.

The passport also records calibration age, the validation report, the terms hash, the model hash, the feature-spec version, the soundprint, aggregate stamps and a previous-passport hash. Passport v2 is signed as installation attestation. The signature does not make the model accurate and does not prove that the object was physically present.

## 10b. Six-take calibration coach

The calibration UI coaches clipping, silence, room noise and unstable level before training. The intended minimum protocol is at least two idle takes, two active takes, one negative/background take and one transition or second-condition take, plus optional held-out validation takes. A heterogeneous set is better than six near-identical recordings. The coach warns when takes may be too similar for a separable model; training still applies the hard data and precision gates in section 8.

## 11. Reproduce and audit

```bash
npm run fixtures        # regenerate synthetic takes + 55s WAV
npm run train:reference # train + leave-one-take-out evaluate
npm run eval:reference  # rewrite docs/evaluation.md
npm test                # includes model/reference assertions
```

The model artifact contains training parameters, dataset hash, feature names, means/stds, weights, bias, policy, metrics, baseline, feature importance, status reasons, limitations and the optional acoustic passport. Any change to the feature spec requires a new version; a model with a mismatched spec is refused.

## 12. Ownership and license

Original implementation for this project. MIT licensed. No third-party model weights, datasets, fonts beyond open-source font packages, or copyrighted audio are included.

## 13. Open-set rejection (Whirr 3.0)

New models carry an optional `rejection` policy with two thresholds. `minTopProbability` (default 0.55) marks a frame `LOW_CONFIDENCE` when the maximum class probability is weak. `unknownOtherProbability` (default 0.45) marks `UNKNOWN_OBJECT` when the `other` class dominates both idle and active. Both flags are disqualifying, so those frames become free `UNCERTAIN` time through the same hysteresis path as a passport mismatch.

Older models without the `rejection` field remain readable and use the default policy. The bundled synthetic reference model is retrained with the field. No threshold was tuned on physical objects, and the synthetic competing-sound tests demonstrate only that the code path rejects a dominant unknown class; they are not field accuracy evidence.
